summary: Cross-currency remittance posted to suspense GL, blocking next scheduled payout to supplier
description:
Issue summary:
A scheduled payout to supplier 'Greenwave Logistics' (vendor ID V-003412) for invoice batch MARCH-02 was blocked when the payment engine posted the cleared remittance to a suspense GL (4000-SUSP) instead of the designated vendor clearing account (2100-AP). This appears tied to a cross-currency settlement step where the USD -> EUR FX conversion name did not match the ledger mapping key, causing downstream allocation to fail and the upcoming ACH batch to be held by the payments scheduler.

Impact:
- One scheduled ACH payout (net ~USD 38,500) is on hold and shows as pending-cleared in the banking integration UI.
- Finance cannot close the vendor month-to-date balance for Greenwave; month-end reconciliation is impacted for AP.
- Risk of late payment and supplier escalation if not resolved prior to next attempt (scheduled 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC).

Environment:
- Production payments pipeline (payments-service v3.8.1), connected to bank connector 'StripeBank-Prod'.
- Vendor: Greenwave Logistics (V-003412).
- Invoices: INV-2026-0032, INV-2026-0033 (multi-PO allocation across PO-7781 & PO-7785).

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) Finance uploaded remittance file CSV (remit_ref: GW-0310-USD-EUR) via AP portal at 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC.
2) Payments-service consumed the remit file and started FX conversion task using fx-profile 'standard-usd-eur'.
3) Conversion completed but ledger mapping failed: fx-profile label did not match GL mapping key (expected 'USD_EUR_STD' vs received 'standard-usd-eur').
4) The allocation step defaulted to 'suspense' when mapping lookup returned null. Posting created GL transaction to 4000-SUSP and flagged payment as 'cleared-suspense'.
5) Scheduler recognized cleared-suspense and withheld ACH batch until manual review.

Expected behavior:
- FX conversion should map to the configured GL account 2100-AP (or vendor-specific clearing account) and allow normal payout processing.

Actual behavior:
- Posting to suspense account blocked the scheduled payout; finance must manually move the GL entry or re-post with correct mapping.

Logs/attachments:
- Payment service logs (payments-2026-03-10.log) lines 1242-1270 show mapping lookup result: "mapping_key_not_found: standard-usd-eur".
- Bank connector trace id: bank-trace-9a7c3f.
- Uploaded remittance file: attachments/GW-0310-remit.csv (secure).

Business notes:
- Vendor is on a net-30 cadence; missing this payout may trigger expedited freight fees.
- This vendor has multiple POs on the batch; allocation mismatch could cause multi-PO unapplied balances.

Temporary workaround:
- Manual GL reclassification from 4000-SUSP -> 2100-AP for the single transaction allows the scheduler to release the payout. Finance-run manual journal recommended as interim.

Urgent ask:
- Engineering to validate why fx-profile labels are not normalizing to expected mapping keys and provide a hotfix or safe mapping override so the upcoming scheduled batch (2026-03-13 02:00 UTC) will not be blocked for other vendors.
comments: 2026-03-10 12:05 — Claire O'Neill (Finance Ops): Notified vendor and held communications; they requested ETA before initiating carrier hold. Finance requests manual GL move to allow immediate payout.
2026-03-10 13:40 — Diego Ramirez (Payments): Retrieved logs and reproduced mapping miss; looks like recent config name change in fx-profiles. I will escalate to infra.
2026-03-10 15:10 — SRE (Slack #payments): Linked bank-trace-9a7c3f to trace in observability. No downstream network errors; mapping null returned upstream from ledger service.
2026-03-11 09:22 — Claire O'Neill (Finance Ops): Completed manual journal to reclassify transaction and requested scheduler re-run. Scheduler still prevents auto-release until mapping issue fixed.
2026-03-11 11:00 — Diego Ramirez (Payments): Implemented temporary mapping alias 'standard-usd-eur' -> 'USD_EUR_STD' in staging for testing. Need approval for prod alias deploy.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 14:00 — Initial triage: Payment ingestion and FX conversion succeeded; ledger mapping returned null due to mismatch between fx-profile label and GL mapping key.
2026-03-10 16:10 — Hypothesis 1: Recent rename of fx-profile in config (human-friendly slug changed) without corresponding GL mapping update.
2026-03-11 08:45 — Hypothesis 2: ledger-mapping service does a strict string match; it does not consult profile aliases.
root_cause: Ledger mapping is implemented as a strict key lookup against fx-profile labels. A recent change to an fx-profile display slug ('USD_EUR_STD' -> 'standard-usd-eur') was not synchronized to GL mapping configuration, causing allocations to fall back to suspense account.
resolution: 2026-03-12 07:30 — Prod config change: Added mapping alias 'standard-usd-eur' -> 'USD_EUR_STD' in ledger-mapping service config via deploy PR #finance/ledger-mapping-fix. (see related_github_prs below)
2026-03-12 08:00 — Finance completed manual reclass for Greenwave transaction; scheduler allowed payout release and bank connector shows ACH submitted at 2026-03-12 09:12 UTC.
Status: Partial fix — mapping alias prevents new occurrences, but root hygiene requires a stronger mitigation to avoid future slug/name drift.
follow_up_actions: Create a governance task to ensure fx-profile renames require a mapped alias or automated mapping sync (owner: Finance/Payments).
Enhance ledger-mapping service to accept canonical IDs in addition to human slugs to avoid string-drift failures (owner: Payments infra).
Add alert when posting to 'suspense' exceeds threshold (e.g., > $10k in a day) — integrate with PagerDuty.
Run reconciliation sweep for last 30 days to detect similar mapping mismatches and reclass any outstanding suspense postings.
